title: Optional runners.local.toml and runners.cloud.toml override the common runners.toml
description:
OPERATOR, 2026-09-23: 'the config system should support different configs for cloud and local (optional)', and the shape: 'you can either have runners.toml (common), or runners.cloud.toml, runners.local.toml which override if they exist'. Prompted by: 'if a tick is complex you can consider using a claude executor locally. It should be significantly stronger than pi/glm' - while the cloud must never run claude.

THE SHAPE (the operator's):
  .tick/runners.toml         common to every run - as today
  .tick/runners.local.toml   optional; overrides for every non-cloud substrate (auto, herdr, harness)
  .tick/runners.cloud.toml   optional; overrides for the cloud substrate (the container)
With neither override file, behaviour is exactly today's.

SEMANTICS to settle and write down in one place:
  - Same schema in all three files, validated the same way.
  - The matching override is merged over the common file: TABLES merge field-wise; ARRAYS (e.g. [[tier_policy.start]]) are REPLACED wholesale, because a merged list of rules has no meaning anyone wrote.
  - The override is applied LAST - after role and tier resolution - so an override always wins. This closes finding ea1a62d3 by construction: today 84z's comment says 'a tier still the more specific axis', i.e. a tier overlay beats the cloud overlay, so a claude frontier tier would win in a cloud run.
  - A tier defined only in runners.local.toml does not exist for a cloud run, and naming it there is refused with the file it lives in.
  - Which substrate is resolved already (TICKS_SUBSTRATE=cloud in the container; otherwise the local decision) - the file choice follows it, and the run's feed says which files it loaded.

MIGRATION: 84z's inline roles.<role>.substrates.cloud cells move into runners.cloud.toml, and the inline form is refused afterwards with a message pointing at the file - two ways to say one thing is how the two drift.

UPSTREAM: ticks uep (tk's config copy refuses 84z's inline key) - with the inline form gone, tk only needs to leave the two new files alone and document them in the ticks skill's runners-config reference.

FIRST USE, once this lands:
  runners.local.toml:  [roles.implement.tiers.frontier] kind = claude, model = opus, effort = high; [tier_policy] default = strong, ceiling = frontier, step = 1
  runners.cloud.toml:  every role pi on cloudflare-workers-ai/@cf/zai-org/glm-5.3; [tier_policy] ceiling = strong
notes: 2026-09-23 20:26 - 2026-09-23: the local claude ladder WAITS FOR THIS TICK. Putting [roles.implement.tiers.frontier] (claude opus) plus [tier_policy] ceiling = frontier into the common runners.toml was tried and correctly refused by TestRepoRunnersConfigKeepsClaudeOffTheCloud: ResolveOn(cloud, implement, frontier) routed the claude harness into a container, because a tier overlay applies OVER the cloud overlay (ea1a62d3). Once this tick lands, runners.local.toml gets exactly that ladder (verified to derive: attempt 1 -> strong -> pi/glm-5.3, after one failure -> frontier -> claude/opus, capped) and runners.cloud.toml caps the ladder at strong. The operator's rule: claude encouraged locally when stuck; never invoked from Cloudflare executors. The factory gateway's Workers-AI-only allow-list is the physical backstop, now guarded by TestTheFactoryGatewayRoutesWorkersAIOnly.
acceptance_criteria: With no override files resolution is unchanged; runners.local.toml and runners.cloud.toml are each merged over runners.toml for their substrate, tables field-wise and arrays replaced, applied after role and tier resolution; a tier defined only in runners.local.toml is refused in a cloud run naming the file; 84z's inline cloud cells are migrated into runners.cloud.toml and the inline form refused; the run feed names the files loaded; and the full suites pass
